title: Software Developer
content:
Explore a Career as a Software Developer

Software developers design, build and improve the apps, websites and systems people use every day, from games and banking apps to the software that runs hospitals.

What they do

  • Turn ideas and requirements into working code
  • Test and fix problems in software
  • Work in teams with designers, testers and product owners

Skills you will need

  • Logical thinking and problem solving
  • Patience and attention to detail
  • Teamwork and clear communication

How to get there

Common routes include a degree in computer science or software engineering, a digital or software development apprenticeship, or an intensive coding bootcamp. Building your own projects at school is a great way to start.

Where it can lead

With experience you could become a senior or lead developer, a software architect, or specialise in areas such as cyber security, games or artificial intelligence.

title: Registered Nurse
content:
Explore a Career as a Registered Nurse

Nurses care for patients of all ages, helping them recover from illness or injury and supporting them and their families through some of the most important moments of their lives.

What they do

  • Assess patients and plan their care
  • Give medicines and treatments
  • Work alongside doctors and other health professionals

Skills you will need

  • Compassion and empathy
  • Staying calm under pressure
  • Excellent communication

How to get there

You will usually need a nursing degree in adult, children’s, mental health or learning disability nursing. Nursing degree apprenticeships let you earn while you study.

Where it can lead

You could specialise in areas such as intensive care or midwifery, become a nurse practitioner, or move into management, teaching or research.

title: Electrician
content:
Explore a Career as an Electrician

Electricians install, maintain and repair the electrical systems that power homes, schools, businesses and renewable energy projects such as solar panels and electric vehicle chargers.

What they do

  • Install wiring, lighting and power systems
  • Find and fix electrical faults
  • Make sure work meets safety standards

Skills you will need

  • Practical, hands-on ability
  • Maths and reading technical drawings
  • A careful approach to safety

How to get there

Most electricians train through an electrical installation apprenticeship. College courses in electrical installation can also help you get started.

Where it can lead

You could run your own business, become an electrical engineer, or specialise in green technology and smart home systems.

title: Graphic Designer
content:
Explore a Career as a Graphic Designer

Graphic designers use images, type and colour to communicate ideas, creating everything from logos and posters to websites, packaging and social media campaigns.

What they do

  • Create visual concepts by hand or with design software
  • Develop brands and visual identities
  • Present ideas to clients and refine them using feedback

Skills you will need

  • Creativity and a strong eye for detail
  • Using design software
  • Taking feedback and meeting deadlines

How to get there

Many designers study art, graphic design or visual communication at college or university. A strong portfolio of your work matters as much as qualifications.

Where it can lead

You could become a senior designer or art director, move into user experience (UX) or motion design, or work as a freelancer.

title: Civil Engineer
content:
Explore a Career as a Civil Engineer

Civil engineers plan, design and manage the construction of the structures we rely on, including bridges, roads, railways, tunnels, flood defences and water systems.

What they do

  • Design structures and work out how they will be built
  • Assess risks and environmental impact
  • Manage projects and teams on site

Skills you will need

  • Maths and physics
  • Problem solving and creativity
  • Project management and leadership

How to get there

A degree in civil engineering is the most common route. Civil engineering apprenticeships, including degree apprenticeships, are also widely available.

Where it can lead

With experience you can become a chartered engineer, lead major infrastructure projects, or specialise in areas such as sustainable design.

title: Data Analyst
content:
Explore a Career as a Data Analyst

Data analysts collect and study information to help organisations make better decisions, whether that is improving a hospital service, a sports team’s performance or a shop’s stock levels.

What they do

  • Gather and clean data from different sources
  • Look for patterns and trends
  • Present findings with charts and reports

Skills you will need

  • Confidence with numbers and statistics
  • Curiosity and asking good questions
  • Explaining complex ideas simply

How to get there

You could study maths, statistics, computer science or economics at university, or take a data analyst apprenticeship. Spreadsheet and coding skills give you a head start.

Where it can lead

You could progress to senior analyst, data scientist or data engineer, or lead an analytics team.

title: Primary School Teacher
content:
Explore a Career as a Primary School Teacher

Primary school teachers help children aged 4 to 11 learn to read, write, count and discover the world around them, and play a big part in how young people see themselves.

What they do

  • Plan and deliver lessons across many subjects
  • Track pupils’ progress and support those who need extra help
  • Work with parents, carers and other staff

Skills you will need

  • Patience and enthusiasm
  • Organisation and planning
  • Communicating with children and adults

How to get there

You will need a degree and qualified teacher status (QTS). You can train through a teaching degree, or complete a postgraduate teacher training course after any degree.

Where it can lead

You could become a subject leader, special educational needs coordinator (SENCO), deputy head or headteacher.
